# How small can a cancer test get before it stops working?

<!-- Generated by scripts/build_report_page.py from results/*/tables. Do not edit by hand:
     edit scripts/report_template.md and rebuild. -->

Interactive version: **https://lolsripal.github.io/genepanel-shrink/**

## Summary

I trained cancer-detection models on gene expression and shrank the set of genes they could
use from 17,699 down to one, across 19 tasks in four settings:

| Setting | Best 1 gene | Best 10 genes | All genes | 10 random genes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tumor tissue, breast (TCGA) | 0.989 | 1.000 | 0.999 | 0.97 |
| Blood test, lung cancer vs non-cancer (platelet RNA) | 0.84 | 0.90 | 0.96 | 0.74 |
| Lung adenocarcinoma vs squamous (tissue) | 0.973 | 0.991 | 0.989 | 0.90 |

*ROC-AUC, logistic regression, mean over patient-grouped test folds.*

- **Tumor tissue is an easy case.** 1–2 genes match the full model (2 genes at most
  across the four tissue tasks), because hundreds of genes each separate tumor from normal.
- **In blood, panel size matters.** No panel of 500 genes or fewer matched the full model in
  any blood task, and accuracy climbs steadily with more genes.
- **Confounding is large in the blood data.** Hospital plus age, sex and smoking alone (no
  genes) reach AUC 0.93. A real signal remains in the authors' matched cohort (genes
  0.95 vs metadata 0.64).
- **Small panels break first on new data.** A 1-gene lung test that correctly rejected
  95% of normal samples in its own data rejected only 30%
  of healthy lungs from another pipeline (100 genes: 100% → 93%).
- **Telling cancers apart bends the curve too.** Naming 1 of 12 cancer types reaches balanced
  accuracy 33% with 1 gene, 95% with 10 and 98%
  with all genes. Breast subtypes need about 50 genes.

## Methods in brief

- **Validation.** 5-fold CV repeated 5 times (2 for the 12-type task), grouped by patient.
  Gene selection is redone inside every training fold, and a unit test checks that selectors
  never see test samples.
- **"Matches all genes"** means the lower 95% bound of the paired fold-wise AUC difference
  (panel − all genes) stays above −0.01, using the Nadeau–Bengio corrected resampled t-test
  (repeated-CV folds overlap, so naive intervals are too narrow).
- **Selectors:** t-test (ANOVA F), LASSO path, mutual information, recursive feature
  elimination, SHAP on XGBoost, stability selection (50 half-samples). Baselines: 20 random
  draws per size, and the most variable genes.
- **Models:** logistic regression (C tuned by inner CV), random forest (300 trees), XGBoost
  (300 rounds, depth 3), MLP (64-32, early stopping); all class-balanced.
- **Data:** TCGA via UCSC Xena (log2 RSEM+1); TCGA + GTEx via UCSC Toil (log2 TPM+1);
  platelet RNA-seq counts from GEO (log2 CPM+1). Genes are mapped to symbols with GENCODE v23.

## 1 · Tumor tissue (TCGA breast and lung)

1,211 breast and 573 lung samples (tumor vs adjacent normal), plus Stage I tumors only.
The best single gene reaches AUC 0.989 (breast) and 0.999 (lung), while a random
gene reaches 0.70. All four tissue tasks are matched by panels of 2 genes or
fewer. Hundreds of genes each separate the classes, so this ceiling says more about the
task than about the methods. Selected genes are mostly normal-tissue genes lost in tumors
(fat, vessels, alveoli) plus stroma-remodelling genes such as COL10A1 and MMP11.
Details: `results/tables/`, notebooks 01–03.

## 2 · Blood test (tumor-educated platelets)

GSE89843: 779 people (402 lung cancer, 234 healthy, 143 with other diseases).
GSE68086: 285 people (55 healthy, 230 with one of six cancers).

**Panel size matters.** For lung cancer vs all non-cancer, AUC is 0.84 with 1 gene,
0.90 with 10, 0.94 with 100 and 0.96 with all 4,694 genes; 10 random genes give
0.74. No panel of 500 genes or fewer is statistically as good as all genes, in any of
the eight blood tasks.

**Confounding.** Only VUMC contributed both classes. MGH and NKI sent only cancers, UMCU,
AMC and UMEA only controls, and cancer patients are ~17 years older on average.

| Model sees only (no genes) | AUC, lung cancer vs non-cancer |
|---|---|
| hospital | 0.81 |
| age | 0.81 |
| hospital + age + sex + smoking | 0.93 |

- Among people *without* cancer, platelet RNA identifies VUMC vs other hospitals with AUC
  0.90 (n = 60 non-VUMC controls): a site signature is in the RNA.
- Within VUMC only, all genes reach AUC 0.97.
- In the authors' age/sex/smoking-matched cohort, metadata alone gives 0.64, but
  genes give 0.95 (10 genes: 0.91). This is the cleanest evidence of
  a cancer signal.
- For non-metastatic cancer (57 patients), age + sex + smoking alone reach 0.97,
  as high as the gene model (0.97). This task cannot show a cancer-specific signal.

**The authors' split.** Their full-cohort training set (208 people) came from
VUMC (plus some UMCU controls). Trained on it and scored once on their validation set,
cancers from VUMC are detected with AUC 0.95, cancers from hospitals missing from
training with 0.79 (LASSO 10 genes: 0.61). On the matched
cohort's validation set: 0.95 (10 genes: 0.89). The original
papers report AUC 0.94 (late-stage validation, n = 518) and 0.89 (early-stage, n = 106)
[Best et al., Cancer Cell 2017, doi:10.1016/j.ccell.2017.07.004]. Their cohorts are defined
differently, so these are reference points rather than like-for-like comparisons.

**Six cancers (GSE68086).** Any cancer vs healthy: AUC 0.99 (all genes), 0.95
(10 genes). Which of six types: AUC 0.87, balanced accuracy 60% (all
genes), AUC 0.79 with 10 genes. The paper reports 96% and 71% accuracy
[Best et al., Cancer Cell 2015, doi:10.1016/j.ccell.2015.09.018]. Healthy controls come only
from three of six processing batches; restricting to those batches gives similar results
(`results/blood/tables/summary.csv`, `GSE68086_batch234`).

Calibration and decision curves (out-of-fold predictions) are in
`results/blood/tables/calibration.csv` and `decision_curve.csv`.

## 3 · Healthy controls and external validation (UCSC Toil: TCGA + GTEx)

**Study-effect control.** TCGA adjacent-normal vs GTEx healthy tissue, two kinds of
"normal", separate with AUC 1.000 using 2 genes; a random single gene gives
0.72. Tumor-vs-GTEx results in this chapter therefore partly measure the study a
sample came from, not only cancer.

**Frozen models on a new pipeline.** Models trained as in chapter 1 (Xena, tumor vs adjacent
normal) are applied unchanged to Toil tumors from held-out patients plus GTEx healthy tissue.
Genes are matched to the training scale using samples present in both pipelines, from
training patients only (LASSO panels):

| | AUC, own data | AUC, new data | Normals rejected, own data | Healthy rejected, new data |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lung, 1 gene | 0.98 | 0.91 | 95% | 30% |
| Lung, 10 genes | 1.00 | 0.98 | 98% | 72% |
| Lung, 100 genes | 1.00 | 1.00 | 100% | 93% |
| Breast, 1 gene | 0.98 | 0.98 | 92% | 88% |
| Breast, 10 genes | 1.00 | 1.00 | 100% | 100% |
| Breast, 100 genes | 1.00 | 1.00 | 100% | 97% |

Ranking (AUC) mostly survives, but the decision threshold does not, and the smallest panels
lose the most. Without harmonization, thresholds fail almost completely
(`results/external/tables/external.csv`, setting `external_raw`).

## 4 · Harder tasks

| Task | Best 1 gene | Best 10 genes | All genes | Smallest matching panel |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lung adenocarcinoma vs squamous (AUC) | 0.973 | 0.991 | 0.989 | 5 |
| Breast PAM50, 5 subtypes (balanced accuracy) | 54% | 82% | 83% | 50 |
| 12 cancer types (balanced accuracy; chance 8%) | 33% | 95% | 98% | 10 |

What sets the panel size is how distinct the groups are, not how many there are. Twelve
tissues of origin each have lineage genes (TG thyroid, NKX3-1 prostate, GFAP brain, GATA3
breast/bladder), so ~10 genes suffice. Five breast subtypes shade into each other, so they
need ~50. Selected genes are textbook markers (ERBB2, ESR1, FOXA1, FOXC1 for PAM50; KRT5,
DSG3 for squamous lung), with far more PubMed support than random genes
(`results/harder/tables/pubmed_summary.csv`).

## 5 · Models

Across tasks the four models land close together. Logistic regression is best with all genes
in 15 of the 19 tasks, and where another model wins, it is by at most 0.003 AUC. See the model table on the web page or `results/*/tables/summary.csv`.

## 6 · Biology

Consensus panels (genes chosen most often across folds and methods) are in
`results/*/tables/consensus.csv`. In tissue they are lost normal-tissue genes and tumor-stroma
genes. In the six-cancer blood study they are T-cell genes (CD27, IL7R, TRBC2), which points
to immune or white-cell differences rather than platelet changes. Lung-cancer blood panels
include platelet and cytoskeleton genes (CFL1, ITGB3, TIMP1). After a false-discovery-rate
correction over all panels tested, tissue and blood panels are **not** enriched for OncoKB
cancer genes (0 of 202 and 0 of 393 panels), while breast-subtype and tissue-of-origin
panels are (20 of 158), because subtypes are defined by drivers such as ESR1, ERBB2 and
FOXA1. Detection panels pick genes with big, consistent expression changes, and those are
mostly not drivers.

## 7 · What it means

**How much biological information can we remove?** In tumor tissue, nearly all of it, but
only because the task is easy. In blood, the realistic early-detection setting, removing
genes below about 100 costs accuracy, and small panels are also the first to break when the
data change.

## Limitations

- Public, retrospective data. Blood cohorts are small, especially for early-stage cancer (57).
- Hospital and age are entangled with cancer status in GSE89843; the matched cohort helps but
  is small (263 people).
- TCGA vs GTEx differences are partly technical (chapter 3's study-effect control).
- Corrected CV intervals still come from one population per dataset; only chapter 3 and the
  authors' split test transfer to new data.
